caption:
A former Plaud executive just raised $26 million for Ambi, an AI assistant that can listen in the background all day.

It runs on iPhone, Mac and Apple Watch, surfaces suggestions during meetings, and a wearable is on the way.

Would you let an AI listen to your whole workday?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechCrunch, Mistlabs · Photos: Ambi, Wikimedia Commons

slides.headline: Ex-Plaud exec raises *$26M* for an AI that listens to you all day

slides.heading: Meet *Ambi*
paras: Peter Mo, a former executive at AI note-taker maker Plaud, launched Ambi on Monday. His San Francisco startup, Mistlabs, has raised $26 million.
Luminous Ventures and electronics manufacturer Huaqin backed the funding.

slides.heading: How it *works*
paras: Ambi runs on iPhone, Mac and Apple Watch. Like a meeting note-taker, it listens, but users can let it run all day to capture context.
It pulls from calendars, meetings, notes and the web to surface suggestions during a meeting, before anyone asks.

slides.heading: A *wearable* is next
paras: Mistlabs plans a standalone device with a screen, speaker, camera and microphones. The company says the new money will go toward it.
It also plans agent-to-agent features that would let Ambi assistants share context and help negotiate during meetings.

slides.heading: The *privacy* question
paras: All-day listening is off by default, and Ambi says it does not store recordings. It has not said which encryption it uses.
People nearby may not know they are being recorded.

paras.t: Mo told TechCrunch the industry has not solved that problem yet.

slides.hook: Always-on AI assistants are arriving fast. We cover every launch that matters.
